title: Messiah Lord! Who, Wont to Dwell
description: Messiah Lord! Who, Wont to Dwell in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Reginald Heber wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 222 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Holy Guest”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Mes-si-ah Lord! who, wont to dwell In low-ly shape and cot-tage cell, Didst not re-fuse a guest to be At Ca-na's poor fes-tiv-i-ty.

lines: Messiah Lord! who, wont to dwell
In lowly shape and cottage cell,
Didst not refuse a guest to be
O when our soul from care is free,
Then, Saviour, would we think on thee;
And, seated at the festal board,
In fancy's eye behold the Lord.
Then may we seem, in fancy's ear,
And think, — "if now his searching view
Each secret of our spirit knew!"
So may such joy, chastised and pure,
Beyond the bounds of earth endure;
Nor pleasure in the wounded mind
Shall leave a rankling sting behind.

licence: Public domain: Reginald Heber died in 1826.
credits: Words by Reginald Heber (1783–1826), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
